questions.question: What is the core invariant of a production agentic AI system?
options: The model may propose steps, but deterministic runtime controls decide what can execute, persist, retry, and stop.
Every task must be delegated to more than one model.
A tool call is trustworthy when the model explains why it selected the tool.
The run is complete whenever the model says it succeeded.
questions.explanation: The model proposes under uncertainty. Runtime authorization, state, budget, validation, and stop controls enforce the real boundary.

questions.question: A write tool times out after the remote service may have committed. What should the runtime do before retrying?
options: Replay immediately with a new operation ID.
Ask the model whether the first call probably worked.
Reconcile authoritative state by the stable operation or idempotency key.
Increase the model's step budget.
questions.explanation: The result is ambiguous. Reconciliation distinguishes a lost acknowledgement from a failed mutation and prevents duplicate effects.

questions.question: Why is a tool result treated as untrusted data?
options: Every tool result is factually wrong.
External content can contain prompt injection or authority claims that must not become executable instructions.
Tools cannot return structured data.
Only user messages can influence an agent loop.
questions.explanation: A valid transport response can still contain attacker-controlled or irrelevant instructions. Schema, provenance, policy, and authorization checks remain necessary.

questions.question: Which approval design best protects a high-impact mutation?
options: Ask the model to approve its own proposal.
Show a generic confirmation generated from raw tool text.
Pause durable state and show canonical tool name, arguments, scope, and consequence to an authorized reviewer.
Approve every future call to the tool after one successful run.
questions.explanation: The reviewer needs exact, trusted details for the pending effect. Approval must bind to that call and survive pause and resume safely.

questions.question: Which evidence most directly verifies agent task success?
options: The final response sounds confident.
The trace contains many model turns.
The authoritative environment reached the declared success state without policy violations.
The model used every available tool.
questions.explanation: A trajectory is diagnostic evidence, but outcome grading checks whether the intended external state actually exists.

questions.question: When should a team prefer a deterministic workflow over an open agent loop?
options: When the steps and branches are known and ordinary code can enforce them clearly.
Whenever a task uses any unstructured text.
Only when no model API is available.
When the workflow has high-impact side effects.
questions.explanation: Known paths are usually easier to test, authorize, observe, and recover with deterministic orchestration. Add agentic planning only where it provides measured value.
